The illustrious Bhairava said:
Victory to you, O Goddess Mālinī, stainless and destroyer of impurity!

Victorious is you, the supreme power of primordial wisdom (parājñānaśakti), who has emerged from the manifestation of the light born of the Nirvāṇa of the ultimate reality; you are the auspicious Māyākriyā,
appearing as a straight line and again in the form of a coil like a sleeping lord of serpents.
O Lord, you are celebrated as the power of sound (nāda-śakti);
you are radiant, the embodiment of light, and your essential nature is Śiva. You are named Jyeṣṭhā, Vāmā, Raudrī, and Manonmanī.
The Drop (bindu) is the Maiden (vadhūtā), the Half-Moon (ardhacandra) is the state of having been made;

the Triangle (trikoṇa) is the syllable *aum*, the letter *ī*, and the letter *o*. Having attained the state of *saṃdyojya* and *ījita*, she whose nature is speed (*tvarā*) abides in the form of the Yoni (*bhaga*).
From the beginning up to the end of *kṣa*, she exists as the nature of the Womb (*yoni*); she is the Awakener of Śrīkaṇṭha and likewise the Mother of Rudra.

You are the power of the mantra (*mantaśakti*), the auspicious one (*sūśukṃsā*), the one who honors the gods of the three forms (*trīmūrtyamarīśārcinī*), the one whose nature is the lunar days (*tithīśātmikā*), the one who has become Sthāṇu (*sthāṇubhūtā*), and Hara (*harā*).

You are the one who honors the Lord of the Rudras (*ṛṃṭhiśa*), the one whose nature is the Lord of the Bhūtas (*bhautīśa*), and the one who follows Śadyojāta (*saśadyātmikā*). You are worshipped for the sake of grace (*anugrahe*) by Mahāsena, whose limbs are marked by the *kṛla* syllable (*krulaśāṅga*), as the consort of enjoyment (*saṃbhoginī*). You are the end of the sixteen vowels (*ṣoḍaśāntā*), the one who has leaped into the motionless body of the mass of the immortal drop (*mṛtābindusandohanispandadehaplūtā*).

O Śeṣaśamyakā, bestower of supreme bliss and the happiness of nirvāṇa; O Bhairavī, whose power is the play in the garden of Bhairava; O Supreme Mālinī, worshipped by Rudramātā; O Rudraśakti, Khagī, Siddhi, Yogīśvarī, Mother of Siddhis, the All-pervasive One, Sabdarāśī, Yoginī, Ārṇavī, Vāgviśuddhā, and Śivā.

You are Siddhivāgeśvarī, Mātṛkā, Siddhi, Icchā, Kriyā, Maṅgalā, Siddhilakṣmī, Vibhūti, Saṃbhūti, Gati, and she who is called Śāśvatā; you are Nārāyaṇī, Raktacaṇḍā, Karālekṣaṇā, Bhīmarūpā, Mahocchuṣmā, Yogapriyā, Jayantī, Ajitā, Rudrasaṃmohinī, and the goddess known as Navātmā.

O Goddess, you are worshipped by mantra-practitioners who follow the path of mantras, who have abandoned their attachments, who are devoted to the heroes and the Pātāla, and who are deeply faithful, with the five nectars and divine drinks and festivals;
and by those born of one, two, three, four, five, six, or seven births, whether they be humans or non-humans, such as the Munḍas, Kaṅkālas, and Kāpālikas.

O you who delight in wine and meat, you satisfy yourself with auspicious yet worthless things; by those who possess the power of mantras and spells, who observe vows and subsist on [impure] food, and by the Muṇḍakas, Kāpālikas, and Kāpālinas who have embraced divine conduct— by these who utter the syllables of mantra such as *namaḥ*, *oṃ*, *svāhā*, *svadhā*, *vauṣaṭ*, *vaṣaṭ*, *hūṃ*, and *phaṭ*.

O Goddess, bestower of yogic accomplishments, you are worshipped by yogis and yoginīs gathered in melāpas, by practitioners of mantras and reciters of spells who hold protective cords in their left hands, by spiritual sons, by mothers, by those initiated into maṇḍalas, and by those who delight in the play of Rudra;
you are filled with affection for him whose eyes are like lotus petals.

Established in heaven and the intermediate space, the destroyer of the seven netherworlds, the Siddhidevī who grants boons— whosoever, being pure, recites this *Daṇḍaka* once, twice, four, five, six, seven, or eight times a day,
and always remembers her with devotion, that man shall [be unharmed] even amidst fire, weapons, the ocean, or on the peak of a mountain.

O Goddess, beloved of Mahālakṣmī, you feel affection for your sons; yet those who steal gold, those addicted to gambling, and those defiled by the great sins of killing Brahmins or cows— when they remember your face, which resembles the full moon and is adorned with shimmering divine jewels and beautiful earrings that rub against their cheeks— they are released from their bonds.

O Goddess Mahākālī, who art like the fire of time (Kālāgni), those bound with firm bonds and serpent-nooses, and whose arms, thighs, and toes are crushed, are liberated from terrible great diseases by chanting Your names and by remembering Your two lotus feet.
O Bhairavī, Mother of all heroes, whose crown is like a garland of bees upon the heads of Skanda, Brahmā, Indra, Candra, and Arka, and who is tawny with the filaments of the lotus—
Bhairava has come to you for refuge; forgive my offense, O Śivā, forgive my offense!
Having praised her thus, O Great Goddess, by the high-souled Bhairava,
